# The Completion Threshold for Vietoris–Rips Complexes

This file proves the *completion threshold* theorem for Vietoris–Rips complexes:
the Vietoris–Rips complex of a finite (pseudo)metric space at scale `ε` becomes the
**full simplex** (every finite subset is a face) exactly when `ε` is at least the
largest pairwise distance — the tropical (min-plus) "birth sum" `tropBirthSum`.

The development is deliberately thin: it reuses the abstract-simplicial-complex and
clique-complex API from `Catalog.Geometry.CliqueComplexFlag` and the metric Rips graph
from `Catalog.Applications.PoincareData.MetricFiltration`, adding no new abstraction
layer for simplicial complexes.

## Main results

* `fullComplex`                       — the simplicial complex whose faces are *all* finite subsets.
* `cliqueComplex_eq_full_iff`         — `cliqueComplex G = fullComplex ↔ G = ⊤`
                                        (a clique complex is the full simplex iff the graph is complete).
* `vietorisRipsGraph_eq_ripsGraph`    — the symmetric Vietoris–Rips graph of `dist` is the metric Rips graph.
* `ripsGraph_eq_top_iff`              — the Rips graph is complete iff every distinct pair is within `ε`.
* `tropBirthSum`                      — the tropical birth sum: the maximal pairwise distance.
* `ripsGraph_eq_top_iff_tropBirthSum` — Rips-graph completeness at scale `ε` iff `tropBirthSum α ≤ ε`.
* `vietorisRips_eq_full_iff`          — `vietorisRips dist ε = fullComplex ↔ ∀ x y, x ≠ y → dist x y ≤ ε`.
* `vietorisRips_eq_full_iff_tropBirthSum`
                                      — the headline threshold: `vietorisRips dist ε = fullComplex ↔ tropBirthSum α ≤ ε`.

## Implementation notes

The references `Catalog/FINAL/Bridges/RipsTropicalCompletion.lean` named in the original
task do not exist in this catalog; the tropical threshold characterization is therefore
proved here directly (`ripsGraph_eq_top_iff_tropBirthSum`) from the metric Rips graph API.
The combinatorial pivot `cliqueComplex_eq_full_iff` is exactly the extensional
"every 2-set is an edge ⇔ graph is complete" argument suggested by the task.
-/
import Mathlib
import Catalog.Geometry.CliqueComplexFlag
import Catalog.Applications.PoincareData.MetricFiltration

open Finset

namespace CliqueComplexFlag

open scoped Classical

universe u
variable {V : Type u}

/-! ## The full simplicial complex -/

/-- The **full complex** on a vertex type `V`: every finite subset is a face. -/
def fullComplex (V : Type u) : ASC V where
  faces := Set.univ
  down_closed := by intro s t _ _; exact Set.mem_univ s

@[simp] theorem mem_fullComplex {s : Finset V} : s ∈ (fullComplex V).faces ↔ True := by
  simp [fullComplex]

/-! ## The combinatorial completion lemma -/

/-- **A clique complex is the full simplex iff the underlying graph is complete.**

Forward: every two-element set is a face of `fullComplex`, hence a clique, hence an edge.
Reverse: in the complete graph `⊤` every finite set is pairwise adjacent, i.e. a clique. -/
theorem cliqueComplex_eq_full_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    cliqueComplex G = fullComplex V ↔ G = ⊤ := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    ext u v
    rw [SimpleGraph.top_adj]
    constructor
    · exact fun a => G.ne_of_adj a
    · intro hne
      have hmem : ({u, v} : Finset V) ∈ (cliqueComplex G).faces := by
        rw [h]; trivial
      rw [mem_cliqueComplex] at hmem
      exact (isClique_pair hne).1 hmem
  · intro h
    subst h
    apply ASC.ext
    ext s
    simp only [mem_cliqueComplex, mem_fullComplex, iff_true]
    rw [SimpleGraph.isClique_iff]
    intro u _ v _ huv
    exact (SimpleGraph.top_adj u v).mpr huv

/-! ## The metric Vietoris–Rips graph is the Rips graph -/

/-- The symmetric Vietoris–Rips graph of the genuine distance function coincides with the
metric `ripsGraph` from `MetricFiltration`. -/
theorem vietorisRipsGraph_eq_ripsGraph {α : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] (ε : ℝ) :
    vietorisRipsGraph (fun x y => dist x y) ε = ripsGraph α ε := by
  ext x y
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, h1, _⟩
    exact ⟨hne, h1⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h⟩
    refine ⟨hne, h, ?_⟩
    show dist y x ≤ ε
    rw [dist_comm]; exact h

/-! ## Completeness of the Rips graph -/

/-- The metric Rips graph at scale `ε` is complete iff every pair of distinct points is
within distance `ε`. -/
theorem ripsGraph_eq_top_iff {α : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] (ε : ℝ) :
    ripsGraph α ε = ⊤ ↔ ∀ x y : α, x ≠ y → dist x y ≤ ε := by
  constructor
  · intro h x y hxy
    have hadj : (ripsGraph α ε).Adj x y := by
      rw [h]; exact (SimpleGraph.top_adj x y).mpr hxy
    exact hadj.2
  · intro h
    ext x y
    rw [SimpleGraph.top_adj]
    constructor
    · exact fun a => a.1
    · intro hne; exact ⟨hne, h x y hne⟩

/-! ## The tropical birth sum -/

/-- The finset of ordered pairs of distinct points. -/
noncomputable def distinctPairs (α : Type*) [Fintype α] : Finset (α × α) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun p => p.1 ≠ p.2)

theorem mem_distinctPairs {α : Type*} [Fintype α] {p : α × α} :
    p ∈ distinctPairs α ↔ p.1 ≠ p.2 := by
  simp [distinctPairs]

/-- On a space with at least two points, there is a distinct pair. -/
theorem distinctPairs_nonempty (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [Nontrivial α] :
    (distinctPairs α).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := exists_pair_ne α
  exact ⟨(x, y), by rw [mem_distinctPairs]; exact hxy⟩

/-- The **tropical birth sum** of a finite (pseudo)metric space: the tropical (min-plus)
sum — i.e. the maximum — of the birth times `dist x y` over distinct pairs `x ≠ y`.
This is the scale at which the full simplex is born. -/
noncomputable def tropBirthSum (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Nontrivial α] : ℝ :=
  (distinctPairs α).sup' (distinctPairs_nonempty α) (fun p => dist p.1 p.2)

/-- `tropBirthSum α ≤ ε` is exactly the statement that every distinct pair is within `ε`. -/
theorem tropBirthSum_le_iff {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Nontrivial α] {ε : ℝ} :
    tropBirthSum α ≤ ε ↔ ∀ x y : α, x ≠ y → dist x y ≤ ε := by
  rw [tropBirthSum, Finset.sup'_le_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h x y hxy
    exact h (x, y) (by rw [mem_distinctPairs]; exact hxy)
  · intro h p hp
    rw [mem_distinctPairs] at hp
    exact h p.1 p.2 hp

/-- **Tropical completion threshold for the Rips graph.** The Rips graph at scale `ε` is
complete exactly when `tropBirthSum α ≤ ε`. -/
theorem ripsGraph_eq_top_iff_tropBirthSum
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [PseudoMetricSpace α] [Nontrivial α] (ε : ℝ) :
    ripsGraph α ε = ⊤ ↔ tropBirthSum α ≤ ε := by
  rw [ripsGraph_eq_top_iff, tropBirthSum_le_iff]

/-! ## The Vietoris–Rips completion threshold -/

theorem vietorisRips_eq_full_iff {α : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace α] (ε : ℝ) :

  rw [cliqueComplex_eq_full_iff, vietorisRipsGraph_eq_ripsGraph, ripsGraph_eq_top_iff]

    vietorisRips (fun x y => dist x y) ε = fullComplex α ↔ tropBirthSum α ≤ ε := by
  rw [vietorisRips_eq_full_iff, tropBirthSum_le_iff]

  (`CarrierHom`) form a category (`id_comp`, `comp_id`, `comp_assoc`), `OpTree.map` is
  functorial on trees (`map_eval`), depth is non-increasing along morphisms

  tree-depth of a cost-`c` balanced tower equals the step count of a Hensel/Newton
  certificate, with p-adic precision `p^{c·n}` (`cost_tower_precision`,

The unifying slogan, now proved along four new axes:

> **height is the only cost** — it saturates Kraft, it refines node-by-node into the
> weighted height, it is natural along carrier morphisms, and it *is* p-adic precision.

---

## D11 — Weighted Huffman optimum for mixed-cost carriers

**Conjecture.** Fix a leaf multiset `L` and an assignment of node costs in `{0,1}`.  The
minimum of `MTree.eval` over all flag-annotated trees on `L` equals a *weighted Huffman
optimum*: the smallest `D` such that `∑_{ℓ∈L} 2^{value(ℓ) − D} ≤ 1`, where only unit-cost
(`true`) nodes contribute to the exponent.  When all nodes are unit-cost this is the ordinary
tropical Kraft/Huffman optimum of D7; when all nodes are idempotent the optimum collapses to

*The key insight is* that `kraft_eq_one` and `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight` are the two
halves of a single saturation phenomenon: the Kraft identity is exactly the statement that a
*unit-cost* tree spends one bit of "mass" per level, while the weighted-height bound shows
idempotent nodes spend none — so a mixed tree's optimum is governed by a Kraft sum that only
counts the unit nodes.

piece is the Huffman *construction* matching the lower bound — a concrete recursion already

**Conjecture.** The cycle-1/cycle-2 optimality sandwich `⌈log₂ leaves⌉ ≤ height ≤ leaves − 1`

reassociation in the source maps to an optimal reassociation in the target, and the median

*The key insight is* that `map_eval` makes evaluation a natural transformation and
`height_map` shows height is a *morphism invariant* — so every height-based optimality
statement is automatically functorial, and the bridge is not just a bound but a structure-
preserving 2-functor.

*Why now?* `bound_natural`, `map_eval`, and `height_map` (all proved this cycle) supply
exactly the naturality squares; what remains is to bundle them into a `CategoryTheory.Functor`
and exhibit `mkBalanced` as a `NatTrans`, reusing `optimal_height_attained`.

**Conjecture.** Among all functions `Φ` assigning to a flag-annotated tree an overhead

-- NEW_FILE: ed49bc02_retry1_aristotle/Catalog/Bridges/OpTreeKraft.lean
import Mathlib

/-!
# Binary combination trees (`OpTree`) and the Kraft identity

This file defines binary combination trees `OpTree K` whose leaves carry a label of
type `K`, together with basic structural measures (number of leaves, height, maximum
leaf depth, list of leaf depths) and proves:

* `numLeaves_pos` — every tree has at least one leaf.
* `leafDepths_length` — the list of leaf depths has length equal to the leaf count.
* `maxLeafDepth_le_height` and `height_le_maxLeafDepth` — for these trees the maximum
  leaf depth coincides with the height.
* `kraft_sum` — the Kraft identity: the sum over all leaves of `2 ^ (-depth)` equals `1`.
* `clog_numLeaves_le_height` — a logarithmic bound on the number of leaves.
-/

namespace OpTreeKraft

/-- A binary combination tree with leaves labelled by `K`. -/
inductive OpTree (K : Type) where
  | leaf : K → OpTree K
  | node : OpTree K → OpTree K → OpTree K

variable {K : Type}

/-- The number of leaves of a tree. -/
def numLeaves : OpTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf _ => 1
  | .node l r => numLeaves l + numLeaves r

/-- The height of a tree (a single leaf has height `0`). -/
def height : OpTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf _ => 0
  | .node l r => max (height l) (height r) + 1

/-- The maximum depth of any leaf in the tree. -/
def maxLeafDepth : OpTree K → ℕ
  | .leaf _ => 0
  | .node l r => max (maxLeafDepth l + 1) (maxLeafDepth r + 1)

/-- The list of depths of all leaves in the tree. -/
def leafDepths : OpTree K → List ℕ
  | .leaf _ => [0]
  | .node l r => (leafDepths l).map (· + 1) ++ (leafDepths r).map (· + 1)

/-- Every tree has at least one leaf. -/
theorem numLeaves_pos (t : OpTree K) : numLeaves t ≥ 1 := by
  induction t with
  | leaf _ => exact Nat.le_refl 1
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [numLeaves]
    exact le_trans ihl (Nat.le_add_right _ _)

/-- The list of leaf depths has length equal to the number of leaves. -/
theorem leafDepths_length (t : OpTree K) : (leafDepths t).length = numLeaves t := by
  induction t with
  | leaf _ => rfl
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [leafDepths, numLeaves, List.length_append, List.length_map, ihl, ihr]

/-- The maximum leaf depth is at most the height. -/
theorem maxLeafDepth_le_height (t : OpTree K) : maxLeafDepth t ≤ height t := by
  induction t with
  | leaf _ => exact Nat.le_refl 0
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [maxLeafDepth, height]
    omega

/-- The height is at most the maximum leaf depth. -/
theorem height_le_maxLeafDepth (t : OpTree K) : height t ≤ maxLeafDepth t := by
  induction t with
  | leaf _ => exact Nat.le_refl 0
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [maxLeafDepth, height]
    omega

/-- The Kraft identity: summing `2 ^ (-depth)` over all leaves yields `1`. -/
theorem kraft_sum (t : OpTree K) :
    (leafDepths t).foldr (fun d acc => (1 : ℚ) / 2 ^ d + acc) 0 = 1 := by
  induction t with
  | leaf _ => norm_num [leafDepths]
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [leafDepths, List.foldr_append, List.foldr_map]
    have key : ∀ (s : OpTree K) (z : ℚ),
        (leafDepths s).foldr (fun d acc => (1 : ℚ) / 2 ^ (d + 1) + acc) z =
          (1 / 2) * (leafDepths s).foldr (fun d acc => (1 : ℚ) / 2 ^ d + acc) 0 + z := by
      intro s
      induction leafDepths s with
      | nil => intro z; simp
      | cons a as ih =>
        intro z
        simp only [List.foldr_cons, ih]
        rw [pow_succ]
        ring
    rw [key r 0, key l _, ihl, ihr]
    ring

/-- A logarithmic upper bound on the number of leaves. -/
theorem clog_numLeaves_le_height (t : OpTree K) :
    Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves t) ≤ height t + 1 := by
  induction t with
  | leaf _ => simp [numLeaves, height]
  | node l r ihl ihr =>
    simp only [numLeaves, height]
    have hsuper : Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l + numLeaves r) ≤
        max (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l)) (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r)) + 1 := by
      rw [Nat.clog_le_iff_le_pow one_lt_two]
      have hm : numLeaves l ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l) := Nat.le_pow_clog one_lt_two _
      have hn : numLeaves r ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r) := Nat.le_pow_clog one_lt_two _
      have hm' : (2 : ℕ) ^ Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l) ≤
          2 ^ max (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l)) (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r)) :=
        Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (le_max_left _ _)
      have hn' : (2 : ℕ) ^ Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r) ≤
          2 ^ max (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l)) (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r)) :=
        Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (le_max_right _ _)
      calc numLeaves l + numLeaves r
          ≤ 2 ^ max (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l)) (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r)) +
              2 ^ max (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l)) (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r)) :=
            Nat.add_le_add (le_trans hm hm') (le_trans hn hn')
        _ = 2 ^ (max (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l)) (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r)) + 1) := by
            rw [pow_succ]; ring
    calc Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l + numLeaves r)
        ≤ max (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves l)) (Nat.clog 2 (numLeaves r)) + 1 := hsuper
      _ ≤ max (height l + 1) (height r + 1) + 1 := by
          exact Nat.add_le_add_right (max_le_max ihl ihr) 1
      _ = max (height l) (height r) + 1 + 1 := by omega

end OpTreeKraft

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Valuation-Depth → Tropical Functor (Cycle 3)

This cycle reconstructed the missing combinatorial foundation
`Catalog/Bridges/ValuationDepthTropicalFunctor.lean` (the free combination tree `OpTree`, its
measures `numLeaves`/`height`/`maxLeafDepth`/`eval`, the unit-cost `DepthCarrier`, the
universal bound `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + height` and the sharp lower companion
`⌈log₂ numLeaves⌉ ≤ height`), and then **resolved** two frontier conjectures on top of it:

* `Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/ValuationDepthKraft.lean` — **D7 (sharp tropical Kraft)**:
  the exact dyadic mass identity `∑_{leaves} 2^{-depth} = 1` for every `OpTree`
  (`kraft_eq_one`), the leaf bookkeeping (`leafDepths_length`, `leafDepth_le_height`), and the
  packing corollary `numLeaves · 2^{-height} ≤ 1` (`kraft_card_bound`).
* `Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/ValuationDepthWeighted.lean` — **D9 (mixed-cost height)**:
  flag-annotated trees `MTree` with a per-node `Bool` cost, the interpolating bound
  `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + weightedHeight` (`depth_eval_le_weightedHeight`), and the
  proof that it strictly refines both extremes (`mixed_recovers_unit`, `mixed_recovers_zero`,
  `mixed_recovers_strict`).

The unifying slogan, now proved along two new axes:

> **height is the only cost** — it saturates Kraft *with equality*, and it refines node-by-node
> into the weighted height, with idempotent nodes contributing nothing.

---

## D11 — Weighted Huffman optimum for mixed-cost carriers

**Conjecture.** Fix a leaf multiset `L` and a node-cost assignment in `{0,1}`. The minimum of
`MTree.eval` over all flag-annotated trees on `L` equals the smallest `D` with
`∑_{ℓ∈L} 2^{value(ℓ) − D} ≤ 1`, where only unit-cost (`true`) nodes contribute to the
exponent. When all nodes are unit-cost this is the ordinary tropical Kraft/Huffman optimum of
D7; when all nodes are idempotent the optimum collapses to `maxLeafDepth L`.

*The key insight is* that `kraft_eq_one` and `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight` are two halves of a
single saturation phenomenon: the Kraft identity says a unit-cost tree spends exactly one bit
of dyadic mass per level, while the weighted-height bound shows idempotent nodes spend none —
so a mixed tree's optimum is governed by a Kraft sum that counts *only* the unit nodes.

*Why now?* Both ingredients are freshly proved and 0-sorry this cycle (`kraft_eq_one`,
`kraft_card_bound`, `depth_eval_le_weightedHeight`); the only missing piece is the Huffman
*construction* matching the lower bound, already modelled by `mkBalanced`/`mark`.

## D12 — A converse Kraft realizability for depth lists

**Conjecture.** A finite list `d₁,…,dₘ ∈ ℕ` is the `leafDepths` of *some* `OpTree` if and only
if it satisfies the exact dyadic identity `∑ 2^{-dᵢ} = 1` (not merely the Kraft inequality
`≤ 1`). Thus `kraft_eq_one` is not only necessary but a complete invariant of full binary
combination shapes up to leaf-depth multiset.

*The key insight is* that `kraft_eq_one` already proves necessity; the standard McMillan
construction builds the tree greedily from the sorted depths, and the equality (rather than
inequality) is exactly the obstruction that forces the tree to be *full* — every internal node
binary — which is precisely the `OpTree.node` shape.

*Why now?* `leafDepths_length`, `leafDepth_le_height`, and `kraft_eq_one` supply every forward
invariant; the reverse direction is a single well-founded recursion on `∑ 2^{-dᵢ}` decreasing
by the smallest available dyadic mass, reusing the `numLeaves`/`height` bookkeeping.

## D13 — The mixed-cost weighted height is the unique monotone interpolant

**Conjecture.** Among all `Φ : MTree K → ℕ` for which `depth (eval t) ≤ maxLeafDepth + Φ(t)`
holds for *every* mixed-cost carrier, `weightedHeight` is the pointwise *least*; moreover it is
the unique such `Φ` that is additive across nodes and agrees with `height` on all-unit trees.

*The key insight is* that the per-node refinement of D9 is pinned from both sides
simultaneously: `mixed_recovers_unit` makes a unit-cost witness attain equality at every
`true` node, and `mixed_recovers_zero`/`mixed_recovers_strict` make an idempotent witness
attain equality at every `false` node — together forcing the interpolant node by node.

*Why now?* `mixed_recovers_unit`, `mixed_recovers_zero`, and `mixed_recovers_strict` already
establish equality at the two extremes; an extremal-witness argument over a single mixed node
closes minimality with no new infrastructure.

## D14 — Concrete order-`(1+c)` Householder tower on ℤ_p

**Conjecture.** The balanced-height precision count is realized by a concrete order-`(1+c)`
Householder iteration on `ℤ_p`: an explicit `N_c : ℤ_p → ℤ_p` whose `n`-fold balanced
composition certifies a root to p-adic precision exactly `p^{c·n}`, with `c = 1` Newton's
method and `c = 2` Halley's method.

*The key insight is* that the balanced tree of height `n` evaluates (under the unit-cost
carrier `witnessCarrier`) to depth exactly `n`, so `2^{depth} = 2^n` already identifies the
precision *exponent* with the tree height; attaching a genuine `ℤ_p` contraction turns the
combinatorial count into a certified analytic convergence rate.

*Why now?* The foundation supplies `depth_eval_add_le` and the attaining `witnessCarrier`, and
the **Computation** domain (`Catalog/Computation/PadicValuationDepth.lean`) supplies the p-adic
ultrametric; only the explicit `ℤ_p` iterate `N_c` and its contraction estimate remain.
